description: Spacecraft power system / battery subsystem fault knowledge base for anomaly explanation and solution retrieval.

faults.name: Battery Performance Degradation / State-of-Health Decline
faults.telemetry_signature: Gradual, sustained drift in charge/discharge voltage, current, or temperature over many cycles rather than a sudden spike. Often shows as a slow contextual anomaly (values stay within physical limits but deviate from the learned normal trend).
likely_causes: Normal capacity fade from repeated charge/discharge cycling over mission lifetime
Corrosion of the positive electrode causing diffusion-limiting current and electrolyte dry-out
Cumulative radiation and thermal cycling stress in the space environment
recommended_actions: Trend state-of-health indicators over time rather than reacting to a single reading
Adjust charge/discharge limits or duty cycle to slow further degradation
Flag for ground team review of battery reconditioning or load-shedding strategy

real_world_example.mission: General finding across satellite fleet study
real_world_example.summary: A study of 324 faults across 227 satellites (1994-2014) found power system faults accounted for 26% of all satellite faults, with battery performance degradation and short/open-circuit cell failures among the most common causes.
real_world_example.source: Detection of Voltage Anomalies in Spacecraft Storage Batteries Based on a Deep Belief Network

faults.name: Cell Short-Circuit or Open-Circuit Failure
faults.telemetry_signature: Sudden, sharp step-change (point anomaly) in cell voltage or pack voltage, often accompanied by an abnormal current reading. Distinct from the slow drift of general degradation.
likely_causes: Single battery cell short-circuit failure
Single battery cell open-circuit failure
Charge/discharge circuit fault
recommended_actions: Isolate the affected cell/pack if redundant battery packs exist
Switch charging control to a healthy battery pack via the power distribution unit
Review under-voltage fault protection thresholds to prevent cascading failures

real_world_example.summary: In April 2011 CloudSat suffered a battery anomaly (diffusion-limiting current from positive-electrode corrosion / electrolyte dry-out) that forced emergency mode. Because the battery design did not allow independent cell switching, spare cells could not be used, and it took 8 weeks of recovery operations to regain control.

faults.name: Bus Under-Voltage / Power Collapse
faults.telemetry_signature: Primary bus voltage drops below minimum operational threshold, potentially to zero, for an extended interval. Frequently a cascading/contextual anomaly following another subsystem fault (e.g. attitude loss causing loss of solar pointing).
likely_causes: Loss of solar array pointing (attitude fault) cutting off charging power
Too many components powered on simultaneously, exceeding available power budget
Battery aging combined with unanticipated mission timeline delays
recommended_actions: Trigger autonomous load-shedding of non-essential loads
Command safe mode to preserve power for essential systems (thermal, comms, attitude)
Investigate whether an attitude or power-distribution fault preceded the voltage collapse

real_world_example.summary: On 29 May 1991 Olympus suffered an anomaly leaving it tumbling; batteries discharged, the satellite cooled, and propellant froze. The only transmission was an unmodulated carrier, recoverable only when solar arrays intermittently powered the transmitter.
real_world_example.source: AEROSPACE REPORT NO. TOR-2009(8591)-14, Effective Fault Management Guidelines

faults.name: Lithium-Ion Thermal Runaway / Impedance Shift
faults.telemetry_signature: Rapid temperature rise coincident with voltage instability; a sharp point anomaly in temperature channel usually paired with an anomaly in the corresponding voltage/current channel.
likely_causes: Solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) degradation under radiation and thermal stress
Capacity fade combined with impedance shift from repeated cycling in the space environment
Charging outside safe temperature limits
recommended_actions: Immediately reduce or suspend charging on the affected pack via the battery charge regulator
Use thermal control (heaters or reduced load) to bring the pack back within safe temperature limits
Escalate to ground team for redundant pack switch-over if thermal trend does not stabilize

real_world_example.summary: Lithium-ion batteries used on modern spacecraft remain vulnerable to SEI degradation, capacity fade, thermal runaway, and impedance shifts under space radiation and thermal stress, motivating ML-based monitoring beyond traditional threshold alarms.
real_world_example.source: Spacecraft Anomaly Detection: ML-Based Detection of Li-Ion Battery Degradation in Space Conditions

faults.name: Cell Voltage Imbalance
faults.telemetry_signature: Divergence between individual cell voltages within a pack while total pack voltage stays near-normal - a contextual anomaly visible only when per-cell channels are compared, not in the aggregate bus voltage.
likely_causes: Uneven aging/capacity fade across cells
Faulty cell-balancing circuit
One cell developing higher internal resistance than its neighbors
recommended_actions: Activate active/passive cell balancing if hardware supports it
Reduce depth-of-discharge to slow further divergence
Flag pack for ground review if imbalance keeps widening

faults.name: Overcharge Condition
faults.telemetry_signature: Charge current remains high after voltage has reached the nominal charge-termination point - a contextual anomaly in the current channel relative to the voltage channel.
likely_causes: Charge regulator failing to terminate charging on schedule
Incorrect charge-termination voltage setpoint
Temperature sensor feeding bad data to the charge controller
recommended_actions: Command manual charge termination via the battery charge regulator
Cross-check temperature sensor reading feeding the charge control loop
Review charge-termination setpoints for drift

faults.name: Deep Discharge / Over-Discharge
faults.telemetry_signature: Pack voltage drops well below the safe minimum operating threshold - typically a sharp point anomaly following an unplanned high-load event or eclipse longer than expected.
likely_causes: Unplanned high-power load left active during eclipse
Longer-than-predicted eclipse duration
Under-voltage fault protection failing to trigger load shedding in time
recommended_actions: Trigger emergency load shedding immediately
Verify eclipse prediction model against actual orbit
Review under-voltage protection thresholds and response latency

faults.name: Self-Discharge Rate Anomaly
faults.telemetry_signature: Pack voltage slowly declines during periods with no commanded load - a slow contextual anomaly only visible over many orbits/days of trend data.
likely_causes: Internal micro-short developing within a cell
Electrolyte degradation increasing internal leakage current
Parasitic load left unintentionally powered
recommended_actions: Audit all bus loads for an unintended parasitic draw
Trend self-discharge rate over multiple orbits to confirm it's cell-internal, not load-related
Flag for possible internal micro-short if no external load explains it

faults.name: Battery Charge Regulator (BCR) Fault
faults.telemetry_signature: Charge current becomes erratic or oscillatory rather than following the expected smooth taper - a contextual anomaly with unusual noise/ripple pattern in the current channel.
likely_causes: BCR control loop instability
Component degradation within the regulator circuit
Firmware fault in regulator control logic
recommended_actions: Switch to a redundant BCR channel if available
Power-cycle the regulator to clear a possible logic fault
Escalate to ground team if oscillation persists after power-cycle

faults.name: Battery Temperature Sensor Drift
faults.telemetry_signature: Reported battery temperature diverges from the expected relationship with charge/discharge current and known thermal environment - a slow contextual anomaly in the sensor channel alone.
likely_causes: Sensor calibration drift over mission lifetime
Sensor mounting/thermal-contact degradation
Radiation-induced sensor reading error
recommended_actions: Cross-check against a redundant temperature sensor on the same pack if available
Apply a calibration offset correction if drift is consistent and well-characterized
Treat charge-control decisions cautiously until sensor validity is confirmed

faults.name: Capacity Fade Acceleration
faults.telemetry_signature: Usable capacity per cycle declines faster than the expected aging curve - a slow contextual anomaly visible only in multi-cycle trend analysis, not single-cycle data.
likely_causes: Operating outside recommended temperature range for extended periods
Repeated deep-discharge cycling beyond design limits
Accumulated radiation damage to electrode materials
recommended_actions: Reduce depth-of-discharge to slow further fade
Review recent thermal history for out-of-range operation
Update remaining-capacity estimates used by mission planning

faults.name: Internal Resistance Increase
faults.telemetry_signature: Voltage sag under load becomes larger than expected for a given current draw - a contextual anomaly best seen as a widening voltage-vs-current relationship over time.
likely_causes: Electrode/electrolyte degradation with age
Corrosion at internal cell connections
Cumulative thermal cycling stress
recommended_actions: Trend voltage-sag-under-load as a health indicator going forward
Reduce peak current draws where mission profile allows
Factor into end-of-life capacity planning

faults.name: Cell-to-Cell Connector Corrosion
faults.telemetry_signature: Sudden step increase in measured resistance/voltage drop at a specific cell interconnect - a point anomaly localized to one connection point rather than the whole pack.
likely_causes: Moisture or contamination ingress at a connector prior to launch
Long-duration galvanic corrosion at a dissimilar-metal junction
Mechanical stress/vibration loosening a connection
recommended_actions: Isolate the affected string if pack architecture allows
Monitor for progressive worsening versus a one-time step change
Document for post-mission failure analysis if isolation isn't possible

faults.name: Trickle Charge Failure
faults.telemetry_signature: Pack voltage slowly drifts down during a nominally fully-charged, idle period when trickle charge should be maintaining it - a slow contextual anomaly during otherwise quiet mission phases.
likely_causes: Trickle charge circuit not engaging as commanded
Charge controller misjudging pack as already at float voltage
Wiring fault in the trickle-charge path
recommended_actions: Command a manual trickle-charge cycle to confirm the circuit responds
Verify charge controller's float-voltage logic against actual pack state
Escalate if manual trickle charge also fails to arrest the drift

faults.name: Depth-of-Discharge Limit Violation
faults.telemetry_signature: Discharge depth exceeds the mission's defined safe DoD limit for that orbit/eclipse - a point anomaly flagged against a mission-defined threshold rather than a physical failure limit.
likely_causes: Higher-than-planned power draw during eclipse
Incorrect DoD limit configured after a mission profile change
Battery capacity already degraded below what the DoD limit assumed
recommended_actions: Review load shedding priorities for the next eclipse cycle
Reconcile configured DoD limits against current (degraded) battery capacity
Flag repeated violations as a sign the power budget needs rebalancing

faults.name: Battery Bus Coupling Fault
faults.telemetry_signature: Voltage readings at the battery differ unexpectedly from voltage readings at the main bus during the same interval - a contextual anomaly only visible when comparing two related channels.
likely_causes: Degraded or high-resistance connection between battery and bus
Diode/switch fault in the coupling path
Wiring harness damage
recommended_actions: Compare battery-side and bus-side voltage telemetry directly to localize the fault
Check redundant coupling path if the architecture has one
Treat as a wiring/hardware issue, not a battery chemistry issue, before further diagnosis

faults.name: Charge/Discharge Current Ripple
faults.telemetry_signature: High-frequency noise/ripple appears in the current channel beyond the normal smooth charge/discharge profile - a contextual anomaly identifiable by increased variance rather than a mean-level shift.
likely_causes: Switching regulator instability
EMI coupling from another subsystem onto the power bus
Degraded filter capacitor in the power path
recommended_actions: Check for a timing correlation with other subsystems switching on/off (EMI coupling)
Review regulator switching frequency and loop stability
Treat as a power-quality issue distinct from battery chemistry

faults.name: Thermal Gradient Across Battery Pack
faults.telemetry_signature: Growing temperature difference between cells/modules within the same pack - a slow contextual anomaly visible only when comparing multiple temperature sensors on the same pack.
likely_causes: Uneven heat dissipation due to pack mounting/thermal-path design
Partial heater failure affecting only part of the pack
One cell generating more internal heat due to a developing internal fault
recommended_actions: Identify which end/module of the pack runs hot and check the local heater status
Cross-reference with the cell-imbalance check, since a hot cell often also shows abnormal voltage
Consider load redistribution to reduce localized heating if the cause is usage-pattern related

faults.name: State-of-Charge Estimation Drift
faults.telemetry_signature: Onboard SoC estimate diverges from what actual voltage/current history implies - a slow contextual anomaly in a derived/computed telemetry value rather than a raw sensor reading.
likely_causes: Coulomb-counting error accumulating over many cycles without recalibration
SoC algorithm not accounting for capacity fade
A missed or misread charge/discharge event corrupting the running estimate
recommended_actions: Force a recalibration cycle (full charge/discharge reference point) if mission profile allows
Cross-check SoC estimate against raw voltage under known load conditions
Update the SoC algorithm's capacity assumption to reflect current fade level

faults.name: Relay/Switch Contact Degradation in Power Path
faults.telemetry_signature: Intermittent voltage dropouts or resistance spikes correlated with relay switching events - point anomalies clustered around specific commanded switching operations rather than continuous drift.
likely_causes: Contact pitting/erosion from repeated switching under load
Contact welding causing a relay to stick momentarily
Contamination on contact surfaces
recommended_actions: Correlate anomaly timestamps with commanded relay/switch operations to confirm the link
Switch to a redundant relay/path if available
Reduce switching frequency on the affected relay where operationally possible
